# Forward Deployed Engineer Interview

> The forward deployed engineer loop, the decomposition round, and the loops at five companies. A free guide from DesignGurus.io, in plain Markdown, with no account required.

Each page is short and ends with links to full course lessons and free articles. Each description below is the opening sentence of that page.

## Cheat sheets

- [Common Mistakes in the FDE Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/common-mistakes.md): Most candidates who fail an FDE loop are capable engineers who answered as if it were a software engineer loop.
- [Decomposition Practice Problems](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/decomposition-practice-problems.md): This page gives 14 problem statements for timed practice, each with the first two clarifying questions a strong candidate would ask.
- [Forward Deployed Engineer vs Solutions Architect vs Software Engineer](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/fde-vs-solutions-architect-vs-software-engineer.md): A forward deployed engineer builds a working system for one customer and stays until it runs in production.
- [Four-Week Plan for the FDE Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/four-week-plan.md): This plan uses about 8 hours a week for four weeks, which is 32 hours.
- [Forward Deployed Engineer Interview Question Bank](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/question-bank.md): This page lists 52 questions grouped by round.

## Companies

- [Anthropic Forward Deployed Engineer Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/companies/anthropic.md): The Anthropic forward deployed engineer loop is commonly reported to have six stages over four to six weeks, ending in a final panel on behavior and values that can decide the result by itself.
- [Cognition Forward Deployed Engineer Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/companies/cognition.md): The Cognition loop is commonly reported to have six stages, and four of them simulate customer work.
- [Google Forward Deployed Engineer Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/companies/google.md): The Google forward deployed engineer loop is commonly reported to combine a classic algorithms round, a "vibe coding" round with a specification that changes mid-session, an agentic system design round, and a Googleyness interview.
- [OpenAI Forward Deployed Engineer Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/companies/openai.md): The OpenAI forward deployed engineer loop is commonly reported to include a take-home case study of about a week, staged coding, a system design round built around models, and a project deep dive.
- [Palantir Forward Deployed Software Engineer Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/companies/palantir.md): The Palantir onsite is commonly reported to draw three rounds from a pool of five types, and decomposition appears in nearly every onsite.

## Rounds

- [Applied AI System Design](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/applied-ai-system-design.md): The FDE design round asks for a system that solves one customer's problem, and at AI companies that system usually contains a language model.
- [Behavioral Questions for Customer Work](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/behavioral-for-customer-work.md): FDE behavioral questions ask for evidence that a candidate can be trusted alone with a customer.
- [The Decomposition Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/decomposition.md): A decomposition interview gives the candidate a short, vague customer need and about 60 minutes to turn it into a plan that could be built in weeks.
- [Discovery and Scoping](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/discovery-and-scoping.md): Discovery is the work of finding out who the user is, what decision that user makes, and what data exists.
- [The Forward Deployed Engineer Interview Loop](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/interview-loop.md): An FDE loop usually has a recruiter call, one early technical stage, and an onsite of three to six interviews.
- [The Learning Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/learning-round.md): The learning round measures how quickly a candidate can use something never seen before.
- [Practical Coding](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/practical-coding.md): FDE coding rounds test the code an engineer writes at a customer site: cleaning an export, calling an API, querying a database, and extending a small program as requirements arrive.
- [The Project Deep Dive](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/project-deep-dive.md): In a project deep dive, the candidate presents one past project and defends the decisions in it.
- [The Re-engineering Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/re-engineering-round.md): The re-engineering round gives the candidate several hundred lines of unfamiliar code that contain defects, and asks for the defects to be found and fixed.
- [The Take-Home Project](https://github.com/design-gurus/forward-deployed-engineer-interview/blob/main/rounds/take-home-project.md): A take-home project asks the candidate to build a small working system alone, usually within about a week, and then defend it in a live review.
